before.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 2 & 4 & 12 & -16 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ − 2R₁ and R₃ ← R₃ − R₁ to obtain rows [1, −2, −6 | 12], [0, 8, 24 | −40], and [0, −2, −6 | 9]. Then R₃ ← R₃ + ¼R₂ gives [0, 0, 0 | −1]. This asserts 0 = −1, so the system has no solution.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 2 & 4 & 12 & -16 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 2 & 4 & 12 & -16 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 0 & 8 & 24 & -40 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 0 & 8 & 24 & -40 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y-6z=12 \\ 0x+y+3z=-5 \\ 0x+0y+0z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=-1,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.

Question 1

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[1−2−6122412−161−4−1221]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

a
[1−2y−2z4+zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
b
No solution
c
[1−3y4−zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
d
[12+2y+6z4+zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
e
[12−2y−6z4−zz],z∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to echelon form, we have

M∼[1−2−6122412−161−4−1221]R2:=R2−2R1∼[1−2−6120824−401−4−1221]R3:=R3−R1∼[1−2−6120824−400−2−69]R2:=18R2∼[1−2−612013−50−2−69]R3:=R3+2R2∼[1−2−612013−5000−1].

The corresponding system is now

{x−2y−6z=120x+y+3z=−50x+0y+0z=−1

Since there are no such numbers x,y,z that form a solution of the final equation 0x+0y+0z=−1, we can conclude that our system has no solution.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying a Singular 3x3 System of Equations That Has No Solution
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 2 & 4 & 12 & -16 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 2 & 4 & 12 & -16 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 0 & 8 & 24 & -40 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 0 & 8 & 24 & -40 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y-6z=12 \\ 0x+y+3z=-5 \\ 0x+0y+0z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=-1,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.

before.name: Question 2
before.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].

decision.explanation: The only nonzero row gives x−y+4z=−1, so x=−1+y−4z. Both y and z are free real parameters. Thus (x,y,z)=(-1,0,0)+y(1,1,0)+z(-4,0,1), which is option d.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+4z=-1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
x-y+4z=-1
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

$$
x=-1+y-4z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+y-4z \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$, $z$ (free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1+y-4z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+y[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution of a Singular 3x3 System of Equations with One Pivot
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+4z=-1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
x-y+4z=-1
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

$$
x=-1+y-4z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+y-4z \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$, $z$ (free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1+y-4z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+y[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:
Consider the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=8 \\ -5{x}_{1}+20{x}_{2}-10{x}_{3}=40 \\ \frac{1}{2}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-4.\end{aligned}

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.

Question 3
?

Consider the system
{−x1+4x2−2x3=8−5x1+20x2−10x3=4012x1−2x2+x3=−4. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[1−42−801040012]
b
M∼[12−4800100001]
c
M∼[1−42−800000000]
d
M∼[14−2800000000]
e
M∼[1−42−801300000]
Submit

decision.explanation: Multiply R₁ by −1 to obtain [1, −4, 2 | −8]. Then apply R₂ ← R₂ + 5R₁ and R₃ ← R₃ − ½R₁. Both lower rows become zero, giving the row echelon form in option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=8 \\ -5{x}_{1}+20{x}_{2}-10{x}_{3}=40 \\ \frac{1}{2}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for the system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ -5 & 20 & -10 & 40 \\ \frac{1}{2} & -2 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ -5 & 20 & -10 & 40 \\ \frac{1}{2} & -2 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & -8 \\ -5 & 20 & -10 & 40 \\ \frac{1}{2} & -2 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2} & -2 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution of a Singular 3x3 System of Equations with One Pivot
content.problem:
Consider the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=8 \\ -5{x}_{1}+20{x}_{2}-10{x}_{3}=40 \\ \frac{1}{2}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for the system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ -5 & 20 & -10 & 40 \\ \frac{1}{2} & -2 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$

decision.explanation: The last row represents 0x+0y+0z=10, or 0=10. This contradiction makes the system inconsistent, so it has no solution.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+5y+2z=1 \\ 0x-2y+4z=3 \\ 0x+0y+0z=10\end{aligned}
$$

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=10,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying a Singular 3x3 System of Equations That Has No Solution
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+5y+2z=1 \\ 0x-2y+4z=3 \\ 0x+0y+0z=10\end{aligned}
$$

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=10,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
after.worked_solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y-5z=1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
x+3y-5z=1
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

$$
x=1-3y+5z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-3y+5z \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$, $z$ (free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-3y+5z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+y[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution of a Singular 3x3 System of Equations with One Pivot
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
content.worked_solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y-5z=1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
x+3y-5z=1
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

$$
x=1-3y+5z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-3y+5z \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$, $z$ (free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1-3y+5z \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+y[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
